observations: Both source questions ask for the number of distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a fixed sequence of operands and binary operators, preserving order.
The shared interface gives operands (integers) and operators (+, -, *) with exactly len(operands)-1 operators.
The mathematical object is the set of results over all full binary parenthesizations of the ordered operator sequence; the requested quantity is the cardinality of that set.

The two wrong trajectories both attempted manual enumeration and undercounted; the first also mis-reduced the leading 7-7+5 prefix, and the second correctly reduced 6*7*7 but then enumerated only 14 cases and missed values.

A correct deterministic procedure is interval dynamic programming: for each contiguous subrange [i,j], compute the set of all possible values by splitting at every k in [i,j-1] and combining left/right sets with operator[k].
The final answer is the size of the set for the full range; this is exact and avoids manual enumeration errors.
Potential pitfalls: integer overflow is not a concern for the stated bounds (operands up to 8, values up to 20), but intermediate products can grow; use arbitrary-precision integers.
Duplicate values must be deduplicated at each interval to keep the computation tractable and to count distinct results correctly.
procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters) where parameters has operands (list of integers) and operators (list of '+','-','*'). Let n = len(operands). If n == 1, return 1 (only one value). Build a 2D array dp[i][j] of sets of integers for 0 <= i <= j < n. Initialize dp[i][i] = {operands[i]}. For length L from 2 to n: for i from 0 to n-L: j = i+L-1; dp[i][j] = empty set. For each split k from i to j-1: for each a in dp[i][k] and b in dp[k+1][j]: apply operator[k] to a and b (a+b, a-b, a*b) and insert result into dp[i][j]. After filling, return len(dp[0][n-1]). Use Python integers (unbounded). This exactly computes the number of distinct fully parenthesized values preserving operand/operator order.
uncertainty: The procedure is standard and exact for the stated problem class. The only uncertainty is whether the source questions intend 'fully parenthesize' to include all binary tree shapes (Catalan many) rather than only some restricted forms; the wording and the wrong trajectories' own framing indicate all full parenthesizations, so the DP is appropriate. No other ambiguity affects the count.
